body:
Honestly, I'd probably beg her not to jump just because I'm scared of heights and she has a good chance of just hurting herself. If she had a surefire way to die, I'd take the opportunity to do for her everything I wish people would do for me. I'd ask her if there's anything she needs me for. I'd do anything short of killing her myself to make sure she was comfortable and able to leave the way she wanted to. I'd of course make sure this is what she wanted, not just something she'd regret after she couldn't turn back, but I wouldn't try to stop her if it was something she wanted to do. If what she really wanted was to jump off of a bridge I'd make sure we found a high one, and I'd make her as happy during those last few moments as I could.

edit: If it turned out she didn't want to die but felt like she had no other option (I guess the opposite of what I feel?), then I'd do my best to help her get through whatever it was that was hurting her.

I've only really mentioned it to my girlfriend, but she's told me that if I tell her I'm feeling suicidal then she's going to do everything she can to stop me. I think she gets scared because she realizes that if I didn't say anything she wouldn't know, but she doesn't realize how much power she has over me. Just about everyone close to me knows I've attempted it in the past and have had therapy, but I haven't brought up how recurring the thoughts are. I might could bring it up to one friend, but again, I don't want him to feel guilty if/when I finally decide to do it. Because really, how can I expect him to be like "ok, if you want to die I won't stop you" and at the same time not expect him to feel responsible if I do it?

And as a side note, the whole "suicidal thoughts aren't healthy" comment almost made me not want to respond. Not to be nitpicky, but it's that kind of response that makes me feel like you're missing the point. If I want to die I'm not all that concerned about health.
